description: The console's URL scheme. The hash names the tab (app.js showView) and the query string carries the scope, so a permalink, a reload and a tab switch are one operation. Values are encodeURIComponent-encoded and decoded with URLSearchParams; keys are plain. write() merges into the live query: an empty value removes its key, unknown keys are preserved in place, existing keys keep their order and new keys append. A value write() would refuse is never put in the URL, so anything read() rejects could only have been typed by hand. Tab switches stay on history.replaceState (Paul's ruling C); pushState is never used. Orientation only - the examples are the contract. v2 (S6, 2026-09-17): up to four PAC evidence panes, each addressed by a PREFIXED key (a.source, a.id, a.committee, a.cycle ... d.*) so `cycle` goes on belonging to Graph and "whose cycle is this?" stays answerable. The pane's search text is transient and is never written; `category` carries the committee-type filter in the same spelling Graph uses. A fifth prefix is not a key this module knows, so e.id is preserved in the query and never read as scope. v3 (S8, 2026-09-18): a.map carries the district map's direction ('raised' | 'spent') on each pane; absent means the pane grid is showing. v4 (UI3, 2026-09-19): `studioPane` is RETIRED. Paul removed the N charts strip that addressed it ("Remove the N charts strip, keep the Board"), so no module reads or writes the key any more. It is not dropped: it is an ordinary unknown key, preserved in place by write(), so a bookmark that still carries one opens the ordinary console with the whole navigation visible. v6 (console redesign build 02, 2026-09-22): Graph's comparison. `compare` names the one dimension compared (industry | cycle | company) and that dimension's own key REPEATS, once per pill, in pill order: ?industry=Banking&industry=Credit%20Union&compare=industry. read() still answers the FIRST value on scope.industry (or company, cycle), so every reader older than compare keeps working, and adds scope.compareValues, the ordered values (at most 3, each once). Without `compare`, a repeated key reads its first value only, as before. A `compare` whose key holds fewer than two usable values is dropped into invalid[], and write() never puts one in the URL. `layout=stacked` is Graph's non-default card layout for two scopes; it is never written with three, where stacked is the only layout. Flat keys only, never JSON (D-039).

industry.value: The published industry label exactly as the snapshot registry lists it (S4 HANDOFF: 'Credit Union', 'Property & Casualty Insurance'). Any non-empty string; the label, never the slug. URL-encoded, so '&' survives.

reserved_note: S6's SINGLE-pane keys, superseded by the prefixed set below and never written by anything. S5 writes none of them and write()'s merge preserves any that are present, exactly as it preserves studioPane and a fifth pane's e.* keys. A permalink that still carries them opens the tab with no pane, which is the point of the negative control.

examples.name: graph_permalink_downstream_activity
examples.why: Ruling A(ii): mode=activity is linkable, and the Candidate view select is visible as soon as a report is chosen.

examples.name: chart_studio_permalink
examples.why: Company and cycle arrive as carried filter pills through pendingScope/applyGraphScope.

examples.name: saved_view_permalink
examples.why: saved= opens one saved view through the existing openability()/openView() path.

examples.name: cross_reference_permalink
examples.why: S4's GET /api/cross-reference?industry=<label> selects the newest run for a label.

examples.name: ampersand_label
examples.why: A published label with '&' in it must survive the round trip; this is why values are encodeURIComponent'd rather than handed to URLSearchParams.toString().

examples.name: graph_filters_full
examples.why: Every Graph filter key at once, in the serialization order scope.js writes.

examples.name: write_merge_remove_on_empty_and_preserve_unknown
examples.why: The two write() rules in one example: an empty value removes its key, an unknown key (the retired studioPane, S6's future keys) is preserved untouched and keeps its place. Existing keys keep their order; a new key appends. This is also what keeps an old pane bookmark readable after v4.

examples.name: evidence_two_panes_same_pac_two_industries
examples.why: The lane's own case: DCCC in the Crypto workbook beside DCCC in the Credit Union workbook, which is what the compare strip exists for. Both panes restore from the URL after the listing loads.

examples.name: evidence_four_panes_mixed_sources_and_cycles
examples.why: The ceiling: four panes, an imported file and a saved snapshot side by side, two of them pinned to a cycle, plus the committee-type filter in the bar.

examples.name: evidence_unassigned_pseudo_committee
examples.why: Rows with no committee ID at all are a pane like any other, so the committee rule has to admit the one word that is not a committee id.

examples.name: write_removes_a_closed_pane_and_keeps_the_others
examples.why: Removing pane B writes empty values for b.*, which drops those keys and leaves A and C where they were - the merge rule, applied to the pane set.

examples.name: graph_compare_industries
examples.why: v6, board G1. The Industry chip holds two pills, Banking then Credit Union; the key repeats in pill order and read() still answers Banking on scope.industry.

examples.name: graph_compare_three_industries
examples.why: v6, board G4. Three scopes: the layout is stacked by rule, so `layout` is not written.

examples.name: graph_compare_cycles
examples.why: v6, board G2. The Cycle chip holds 2023-2024 and 2025-2026; cycles are end years, the earlier one first because it was the chip's value when the comparison started.

examples.name: graph_compare_companies_stacked
examples.why: v6, board G3 with Stacked chosen. Two scopes, so the non-default layout is written.

examples.name: write_starts_a_comparison
examples.why: v6. An array writes the key once per value where the key stood, and `compare` appends.

examples.name: write_ends_a_comparison
examples.why: v6. Clear comparison: one value for the key drops its repeats, and an empty compare and layout remove themselves.

examples.name: graph_permalink_downstream_drawer
examples.why: P5. Clicking a PAC in Top organizations narrows the page to it AND opens the drawer beside the panel; the permalink carries both, so the link reopens the same reading rather than a filtered page with no drawer.

examples.name: evidence_map_permalink_spent
examples.why: S8. A map permalink reopens the map it was cut from: the pane is restored first from a.source/a.id/a.committee/a.cycle, then a.map reopens the district map on that pane.

negative_controls.why: v6. compare=industry with one industry compares nothing. The comparison is dropped and the page opens on its one industry.

invalid.reason: compare needs at least two different values of the key it names

negative_controls.why: v6. compare=party names no dimension Graph compares. It is dropped, and the repeated industry reads its first value, as any repeated key without compare does.

invalid.reason: compare must be one of industry, cycle, company

negative_controls.why: v6. layout=sideways is not a layout. The comparison stands; the layout falls back to its default.

drawerDirection=Downstream is not a #graph-direction option value. The drawer must open on a side the server will answer for, so an unusable side is dropped and the drawer falls back to the largest one.

invalid.reason: drawerDirection must be one of Contribution / Other, Support, Oppose, Unknown

negative_controls.why: drawer=../../etc is not a committee id. The value reaches /api/graph as `recipient`, so the shape is checked here rather than trusted from the URL.

invalid.reason: drawer must be a committee id

negative_controls.why: mode=pac is not a #graph-mode option value. A bad permalink must still open the tab, so the key is dropped and reported rather than thrown.

invalid.reason: mode must be one of direct, activity, estimates

negative_controls.why: A two-digit cycle is not the four-digit end year Graph spells.

invalid.reason: cycle must be a four-digit election-cycle end year

negative_controls.why: A non-numeric cycle is refused by the same rule, so the shape of the refusal cannot depend on the value happening to be digits.

invalid.reason: cycle must be a four-digit election-cycle end year

negative_controls.why: An explicitly blank industry is not a scope. It is dropped and reported; the rest of the URL still reads.

invalid.reason: a blank value names no scope, so the key is dropped

negative_controls.why: saved=xyz is not 32 hex, which is exactly what server.py get_view() refuses. The client must not fire a request the server will answer 400 for.

invalid.reason: saved must be a 32-character hexadecimal saved-view id

negative_controls.why: The teeth of the other five: a URL with no query at all invents nothing. An empty scope and an empty invalid[] - not a default industry, not a default mode. This is the control that fails if read() ever starts guessing values the reader did not put in the URL.

A NON-PREFIXED id is one of the superseded single-pane keys. It is not read as a pane id (and never written), so the tab opens with no pane rather than with a pane whose source nobody named. Silently dropped, like studioPane, because it is not this module's key at all.

A FIFTH pane. Four panes are the ruling, so e.* is not a key this module knows: it is preserved in the query untouched and never read as scope, so a hand-edited permalink cannot open a fifth pane through the back door.

b.source=file is outside csv|snapshot, the only two kinds of source a pane can read. Dropped and reported, and write() will not mint it either, so no permalink can ask the client to fetch a route that does not exist.

invalid.reason: a pane source must be one of csv, snapshot

negative_controls.why: A pane cycle must be the four-digit end year, exactly as Graph's `cycle` is; '24' is the same refusal in a prefixed key.

invalid.reason: cycle must be a four-digit election-cycle end year

negative_controls.why: A pane committee with a space in it is not a committee id and not "unassigned"; the client must not fire a select the console answers 400 for.

invalid.reason: a pane committee must be a committee id or "unassigned"

negative_controls.why: S8. a.map=sideways is neither direction the map offers. A bad permalink must still open the tab and its pane, so the key is dropped and reported rather than thrown.

invalid.reason: a pane map must be one of raised, spent
